resultCeiling: This `pass` is an operator-run result. Every launch row here was observed by the operator in a real client and recorded as sanitized facts and digests; the worlds, raw logs, and screenshots were deleted afterwards. A reviewer can recompute the in-gate half — the conformance suites and the JVM harness — and can check that this file's digest matches what `evidence/m3/manifest.json` records, but cannot re-derive the live half from anything in the repository. `manifest.json` closes M3-W7 on that basis and says so in the same terms.
summary: Stock Minecraft Java Edition 26.1.2 launched through Prism on Linux with Ravel's agent, screen artifact, and native bootstrap only. Injected input followed the ordinary title-screen and world-selection path. Five campaigns are recorded here. The surface campaign re-observed, at 33 callable targets, every row the earlier 31-target campaign had left inherited: the three Ravel screens, the configuration round trip including a restart-required setting, the command and saved-data path, and opt-in profiling. Three of those four passed on their own fresh evidence; profiling did not, because the two longest lines on the report rendered only their tails and the sentence naming what the numbers cannot tell apart was unreadable in the real client. That defect is recorded in `profilingSurfaceDefect`, it was fixed by change `npozznqz`, and the caveat re-observation campaign launched the real client against the fixed screen jar and read the whole report. Every line renders in full at every GUI scale this window offers. With that, every required surface stands observed natively and this record is `pass`. One narrower gap remains open and is named in `openGaps`: nothing on the game's tick path marks a tick boundary, so the collectors' tick counter can never leave zero. The summary no longer states that zero — change `lppyxtnz` names `tick-count` among the metrics this build cannot measure — but the measurement is still missing. That six-metric line is the fifth campaign, `profilingReObservationCampaign`: one title-only launch reading the report at both GUI scales against a screen jar and native library hashed before the game started, run because the fifth M3-W8 review round found that the reading which reported `lppyxtnz`'s effect had been written into a campaign whose recorded digests predate it. That finding is answered by observation rather than by rewording; the claim it broke is withdrawn where it stood and made afresh where it can be checked. Nothing here decides whether M3 closes.

rewrite.measuredIn: The three launches of the world round trip campaign each reported `rewrote 15 classes and 33 methods` in the agent's own shutdown report, with 675660, 749397, and 28845 native invocations. The figure above is the second launch, which is the one that both read a stored aggregate and exited through Quit Game.
rewrite.whyTheRefusedLaunchStillRewroteFifteen: The third launch refused the world before it opened and its `integratedServerNeverStarted` is true, so by the criterion in `surfaceCampaign.launchDetail.first.whyElevenNotFifteen` a reader would expect 11 and 27, and its 28845 native invocations against the others' 675660 and 749397 agree that almost no world ran. It reported 15 and 33 anyway, and the reason is the shape of the seam rather than an error. `world.open-persistence` sits on `Minecraft.doWorldLoad`, whose reviewed descriptor takes an already-constructed `net.minecraft.server.WorldStem` as its third parameter: the stem is built before the call, it holds a `ReloadableServerResources`, and that class's constructor instantiates `RecipeManager` and `Commands`. All three were therefore loaded, and rewritten, before Ravel's prologue ran at all. The fourth world-only class is loaded by Ravel itself — `Persistence.saveSeamInstalled` resolves `MinecraftServer` by name on purpose, and `Persistence.read` resolves `SavedDataStorage` to open the storage over the world directory and read the stored aggregate, which is the read the refusal decided on. Refusing a world is therefore not the same shape as never asking for one: a title-only launch loads none of the four and reports 11 and 27, and a refused world load has already loaded all four. `nativeInvocations` is what separates them, because it counts hook traffic rather than classes.
rewrite.worldOnlyTargetsCriterion: A target is listed below when opening a world is what puts it on the path: the six held by the four classes a title-only launch never loads — `Commands`, `ReloadableServerResources`, `RecipeManager`, and `SavedDataStorage` — plus the two ADG-7 persistence seams, which sit in classes the title screen does load and rewrite but which run only when a world is loaded or saved. That criterion is narrower than `unreachable without a world`, and the difference is worth naming: `server.tick`, `server.tick-integrated`, `save.save-everything`, and `save.set-dirty` also never execute on a title-only launch and are deliberately absent, because this list exists to account for what a title-only launch rewrites rather than to enumerate world-gated behaviour. The arithmetic is unaffected, being per class and per rewritten method rather than per reachable target: 15 − 4 = 11 classes and 33 − 6 = 27 methods.

resolvedDeviations.resolution: The accepted second launch used injected input through the ordinary title-screen and Singleplayer world-selection path. It loaded the world-only classes, exercised command and saved-data behavior, saved, relaunched, and verified persistence.

The source-composed production host populated the runtime and configuration stores during premain. The real Mods, settings, and profiling screens opened from the title menu and consumed production Hook data.

Change lwysptxkplzu replaced the classfile API's loading hierarchy resolver with resource parsing, preventing TitleScreen from being defined reentrantly while another class was transformed. Per-class matched-method and failure reporting then reconciled all 15 classes and 31 callable methods with zero transformation failures.

The accepted second launch opened a world, returned through Save and Quit to Title, selected Quit Game, and let both Java and Prism exit naturally. The earlier title-only SIGTERM launches remain historical evidence but are not the passing trial.

profilingSurfaceDefect.whatWasObserved: Two of the seven lines on the profiling report render only their tail. The line naming the metrics no collector can measure appears as `-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint`, and the accuracy caveat appears as `y key is charged for the lookup as well as for its own code.`, which is not a sentence. The other five lines, all shorter, render in full.
profilingSurfaceDefect.intendedTextIsThatBuildsAndNotToday: The two strings below are what the surface campaign's build would have drawn whole, quoted as that build wrote them. That build declared five unmeasurable metrics; `tick-count` joined them later, in change `lppyxtnz`, so the line the screen draws today carries six names and is recorded as observed in `profilingReObservationCampaign.atScaleOne.linesAsRendered`. Nothing below is a claim about the current build.

intendedText.unsupportedMetrics: Not measurable in this build: retained-memory, allocated-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint
intendedText.accuracyCaveat: A mod is charged for host work it calls back into. The window is entry to return, so a mod that asks Ravel to resolve a registry key is charged for the lookup as well as for its own code.

profilingSurfaceDefect.rootCause: The screen draws every line as a non-editable `EditBox` of fixed width. `EditBox` scrolls its visible window to follow the cursor, and `setValue` leaves the cursor at the end of the string, so any line wider than the widget shows its last characters and hides its first. The window was enlarged from 854x480 to 1400x800 and the same two lines stayed clipped, because the widget width is fixed rather than derived from the screen width, which is what rules out a display-size explanation.
profilingSurfaceDefect.notFixedHere: The fix is small and belongs to the screen rather than to this record. It is deliberately not made in this campaign, because changing the screen jar changes its digest, and every row above was observed against the digest recorded in `artifacts`. Re-observation, not a patch landed after the fact, is what would let those rows keep their provenance.

whatTheClippingCosts.unsupportedMetrics: Two of the five metric names were lost outright, not just the label. The build that campaign ran declared `retained-memory`, `allocated-memory`, `cpu-time`, `transferred-bytes`, and `saved-data-footprint` unsupported — five, before `lppyxtnz` added `tick-count` — and the client showed `-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint`, which is the tail beginning inside the word `allocated-memory`. A player reading that screen could not learn that retained memory and allocated memory were unmeasured, and the fragment `-memory` names neither of them.
whatTheClippingCosts.accuracyCaveat: The whole sentence was lost but its last clause. What the screen showed had no subject and read as though some unnamed key were being charged, which is not what the caveat says.

profilingSurfaceDefect.foundBy: the surface campaign, in the real client, at 33 callable targets

fixedBy.description: fix: split the profiling screen's lines to the width it draws them at
fixedBy.mechanism: The screen now splits every line to the width it draws it at before building the widget, using the game's own font (`splitIgnoringLanguage`) against the widget width less the `EditBox` border inset, so no line is ever wider than the box carrying it and no box has to scroll. Splitting spends rows, so the screen also measures the window's row budget and hands it out in a stated order: the summary and the accuracy statement are claimed first and are never cut.

profilingSurfaceDefect.whyThisBlockedTheGate: M3-W6 asks that per-mod attribution accuracy and unsupported metrics be explicit, and M3-W7 asks that every required surface pass natively. Both halves of that M3-W6 requirement failed on the native screen: two of the five unsupported metric names never reach the player, and the accuracy sentence reaches them as a fragment. The screen's own documentation says an unsupported metric is drawn rather than omitted, precisely so it cannot be confused with one that was left out — the clipping reintroduces exactly that confusion for two of them. The report was drawn, so this was not an unreached surface; it was a reached surface that failed. It now passes.

first.whyElevenNotFifteen: No world was opened, and the launch observed the totals rather than the identities: it reported 11 classes and 27 methods, and nothing in it named which of the fifteen classes went unloaded. What follows is derived from the inventory and is consistent with those totals rather than observed by them. Four classes are world-only, so they are the four that would not have loaded: `RecipeManager`, `Commands`, `ReloadableServerResources`, and `SavedDataStorage`. They hold six of the eight world-only targets — `recipe.apply`, `command.perform-prefixed`, `resource.load-server-resources`, and `SavedDataStorage`'s three `save.compute-if-absent`, `save.try-write`, and `save.save-and-join`. The other two world-only targets, `world.open-persistence` and `world.save-persistence`, sit in `net.minecraft.client.Minecraft` and `net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer`, both of which were loaded and rewritten at the title screen, so they are counted among the eleven. That is the whole arithmetic, and it is the derivation rather than the observation: 15 − 4 = 11 classes and 33 − 6 = 27 methods, not 33 − 8. The two totals are what the launch reported; the set of four is the only assignment of them the inventory admits, which is a strong inference and still an inference. This is the expected title-only shape of the same 33-target inventory, and it is recorded because a reader who sees 11 and 27 beside a claim of 33 deserves the reason.

openGaps.profilingTickCounter: `Profiler::tick` in `crates/ravel-observability/src/profiling.rs` is exercised only by that module's own unit tests and has no caller anywhere in the production graph, so the counter it increments can never leave zero in a real launch. What is fixed is the report, not the measurement: change `lppyxtnz` names `tick-count` among the metrics the payload cannot measure, and the screen drops its tick clause for any metric the payload calls unmeasurable. Re-observed live by `profilingReObservationCampaign` against a build hashed before its launch — the summary reads `2 mods entered` and `tick-count` appears in the unmeasurable line. The gap that stays open is that nothing on the game's tick path marks a tick boundary at M3; wiring one is what would put the clause back, with nothing on the screen to change.
openGaps.profilingCommandCounter: Both mod rows read `0 cmd`, and that is an accurate measurement rather than a broken counter. Two independent reasons, each sufficient on its own. The four commands the surface campaign ran were `/scoreboard ...`, which is vanilla and unnamespaced: `Inner::command` in `crates/ravel-bootstrap/src/runtime.rs` requires the root literal to parse as a whole `ContentId`, and `ContentId::parse` refuses a literal with no `:`, so no command work is constructed and nothing is charged. That fall-through is deliberate and documented there — a vanilla command passes untouched rather than being guessed at. Separately, neither mod in the composed host claims a command: neither `ConfigurationMod` nor `SavedDataMod` implements `HostMod::register`, so `route_profiled` in `crates/ravel-loader/src/events.rs` returns unclaimed before it reaches the measuring path. The one test mod that does claim commands is not in the composed host. This is materially unlike `profilingTickCounter`: the increment path from the JNI hook entry through `route_profiled` to `Profiler::charge` exists in the production graph and is exercised by the conformance suite. What has never happened is a real client showing the counter above zero, and this record does not claim it has. Closing that gap is a composition change — put the command-claiming test mod in the composed host and type a namespaced root — not a change to what the collectors do per callback, so it leaves what `profiling-overhead.json` measures alone.

caveatReObservationCampaign.otherScreensInThatJar: The Mods screen and the title-screen entry point ship in the same jar and were passed through on the way to the profiling screen; both looked as the surface campaign recorded them. That is noted as consistency rather than claimed as a re-observation, because their rows were not the object of this campaign.
caveatReObservationCampaign.howProfilingWasTurnedOn: `-Dravel.profiling=true` in the instance's `JvmArgs`, with `OverrideJavaArgs` set true, because Prism silently ignores `JvmArgs` otherwise. There is no in-game toggle; the screen reports the state and never sets it.
caveatReObservationCampaign.buildBoundary: Both digests above were written by change `qovlymtm`, an ancestor of `lppyxtnz`. Every claim in this campaign is therefore a claim about the build `npozznqz` produced and nothing later. Where a later change's effect was published here it has been withdrawn rather than reworded; see `atScaleOne.readingWithdrawn`.
caveatReObservationCampaign.playBeforeReading: The instance's one pre-existing world was opened and played for roughly two minutes so the report would carry real rows. No world was created and none was removed; the instance still holds exactly one.
caveatReObservationCampaign.guiScalesOffered: This window (854x480) offers Auto, 1, and 2, and Auto resolves to 2. Both distinct scales were observed; cycling past 2 wraps to Auto, so no larger scale exists here to test.

atDefaultScale.linesDrawn: Seven: the two summary lines, the heading `What these numbers cannot tell apart:`, and the accuracy statement split over four lines, all readable end to end.
atDefaultScale.whatTheRowBudgetCut: The mod table and the unsupported-metrics line. At scale 2 the window has seven rows, and the screen spends them in its stated order, keeping the summary, the heading, and the statement. That is the documented no-scrolling limit behaving as designed, not clipping: nothing drawn is truncated.

atScaleOne.linesDrawn: The whole report, with both formerly clipped lines wrapped rather than truncated: the two summary lines, the two per-mod rows, the unsupported-metrics line split over wrapped rows, the heading, and the accuracy statement split over four.
atScaleOne.bothLongLinesWhole: The two lines that were clipped before are the two that now wrap. Every metric name this build declares unmeasurable reaches the player, including `retained-memory` and `allocated-memory`, which the clipping used to swallow, and the accuracy statement reads as a sentence from its subject to its full stop.
atScaleOne.readingWithdrawn: An earlier version of this field enumerated twelve lines naming six unmeasurable metrics including `tick-count`, and said the reading was re-observed after change `lppyxtnz`. That was false of this campaign and is withdrawn. `tick-count` enters the unsupported list only in `lppyxtnz`, which changed both `crates/ravel-observability/src/profiling.rs` and the profiling screen, and both artifact digests this campaign records were written before it — so this campaign's build declared five unmeasurable metrics, not six, and no launch of it can have shown the six-metric line. The line count and the per-mod figures published here were a patch landed after the fact rather than a reading, so they are not restated at some other number; nothing in the record now attributes a specific figure to a launch that cannot be shown to have produced it. What this campaign does stand on is `npozznqz`'s effect, which is that both long lines wrap rather than clip, and that is what `caveatRendersInFull` and `unsupportedMetricsLineRendersInFull` above assert. The six-metric line is observed instead by `profilingReObservationCampaign`, against digests taken before its launch.

caveatReObservationCampaign.exitRoute: Save and Quit to Title, then Quit Game; Java exited on its own with no signal.

profilingReObservationCampaign.purpose: Observe the profiling report at both GUI scales against a build whose artifacts were hashed before the game started, so that the unsupported-metrics line — six names since change `lppyxtnz`, `tick-count` among them — is bound to a build that provably produced it. This campaign exists because the fifth M3-W8 review round found blocking finding B-1: the reading that reported `lppyxtnz`'s effect sat inside `caveatReObservationCampaign`, whose recorded digests predate that change.
profilingReObservationCampaign.answers: M3-W8 review round 5, blocking finding B-1
profilingReObservationCampaign.scopeDiscipline: Only the profiling surface at two GUI scales is claimed, plus the title-menu entry point and the Mods screen passed through to reach it. The world round trip, the refused `dataVersion` load, `current_dir()`, staging, the `-javaagent` attach, the configuration round trip, the command path, and the instance scan were not re-run and keep the provenance they already carried.
profilingReObservationCampaign.buildOrder: The three artifacts were built from the working tree, copied into an owner-only private directory outside the repository, and hashed there. The digests below are of that private copy. Nothing was rebuilt between the hashing and the launch, no gate ran in that window, and the same three files were re-hashed after the game exited and were unchanged.
profilingReObservationCampaign.artifactsRetainedPrivately: The three hashed files were left in that private directory rather than deleted with the raw log and the screenshots. That is a deliberate departure from the earlier campaigns, and it is the point of this one: a digest of a build that no longer exists is what made B-1 unanswerable, because `target/` is rebuilt by every gate run and the launched build was gone before anyone asked which one it was. The files are private and machine-local, so their survival buys another reader no checkability — the ceiling stated at the top of this record still holds — but it does let the operator recompute these two digests on demand, which the earlier campaigns could not offer for any build they ran.
profilingReObservationCampaign.artifactReproducibility: class-loader-identity.json carries a reproducible flag per artifact and this campaign did not, which undersold it; it carries one per artifact now, and the flags on the three artifacts above are those. This is the strongest reproducible link in the M3 set. The two jars are built by the tracked build scripts from tracked Java sources and generated stubs, and they come out byte-identical on a rebuild — an M3-W8 round recomputed both from its own fresh build and got exactly the values above, independently of the operator. The native library does not recompute and the flag says so: rustc records the absolute build path in the binary, so the same source built from a different directory differs while being the same code. What the true flags rest on is the tracked Java sources and stubs being the ones the launch built from; nothing in the gate rebinds these three digests, which is the ceiling this record already states at its top, and the retained private copies are what let the operator recompute them rather than a reader.
profilingReObservationCampaign.whatDiffersFromTheSurfaceCampaignBuild: Two artifacts of the three. The agent jar is byte-identical to the one every other row here was observed against, so the hook inventory and the native boundary are the same 33 targets. The screen jar and the native library are both new: the screen jar carries `npozznqz` and `lppyxtnz`, and the native library carries `lppyxtnz`'s change to `ProfilingReport::unsupported()` along with every other change to the Rust graph that landed since the surface campaign, `srwvwzmovwqv` among them. That is why no earlier campaign's digests could stand in for this reading, and why this campaign records its own rather than claiming sameness.
profilingReObservationCampaign.bothSidesOfTheFixAreInTheHashedBuild: The staged native library contains the string `tick-count` and `crates/ravel-observability/src/profiling.rs` lists `Metric::TickCount` as unsupported; the staged screen jar is built from a `RavelProfilingScreen.java` that drops the summary's tick clause for any metric the payload calls unmeasurable. Both halves of `lppyxtnz` are therefore inside the two digests above, which is the thing `caveatReObservationCampaign` could not say.
profilingReObservationCampaign.nativeStaging: Prism owns `<instance>/natives`: it builds that directory during launch and removes it when the game exits, so a library staged beforehand is wiped. The library was copied there from the hashed private directory by the instance's `WrapperCommand`, immediately before it exec'd the java command the launcher had built. The directory was absent before the launch and absent again after it, which is the launcher's behaviour rather than a cleanup step.
profilingReObservationCampaign.howProfilingWasTurnedOn: `-Dravel.profiling=true` in the instance's `JvmArgs`, with `OverrideJavaArgs` set true, because Prism silently ignores `JvmArgs` otherwise. There is no in-game toggle; the screen reports the state and never sets it.
profilingReObservationCampaign.noWorldOpened: No world was created and none was opened. The report's rows come from title-screen hook traffic alone, which is why the per-mod figures are small. The instance's one pre-existing world was not touched and the instance still holds exactly one.
profilingReObservationCampaign.shutdownReport: `[ravel] rewrote 11 classes and 27 methods; 49077 hook invocations reached native code`, in the agent's own shutdown report on the launch's own output stream.
profilingReObservationCampaign.whyElevenNotFifteen: The same title-only shape `surfaceCampaign.launchDetail.first.whyElevenNotFifteen` derives, on the same footing: no world was opened, the totals are what was observed, and the four classes consistent with them are `RecipeManager`, `Commands`, `ReloadableServerResources`, and `SavedDataStorage`, so 15 − 4 = 11 classes and 33 − 6 = 27 methods.

atScaleOne.summaryStatesNoTickCount: The summary line reads `2 mods entered` and nothing else. It states no tick figure, and `tick-count` stands in the unmeasurable list instead, which is `lppyxtnz`'s whole effect on this surface and is what this launch was run to observe.
atScaleOne.bothLongLinesWhole: Every one of the six metric names reaches the player, `retained-memory` and `allocated-memory` included, and the accuracy statement reads as a sentence from its subject to its full stop. The two lines that used to clip are the two that wrap; the six names take three wrapped rows.
atScaleOne.readTwiceWithinOneOpening: The report was read again eight seconds later without leaving the screen and both per-mod rows were identical, so the payload is a snapshot taken when the screen opens rather than a live-updating widget.
atScaleOne.readAgainAfterReopening: Closing the screen and reopening it from the title menu redrew the same twelve lines with the rows advanced from 2323 to 3445 calls and from 252450 to 375684 ns for `configuration` and 109763 to 159415 ns for `saved_data`. That is what tells a live report apart from a rendered constant, and it is the sense in which the counts advance: across openings, not within one.

profilingReObservationCampaign.guiScaleRestored: The scale was cycled 1 → 2 → Auto and left on Auto, the value the instance's options held before the launch, read back on the Video Settings screen.
profilingReObservationCampaign.exitRoute: Quit Game from the title menu; Java exited on its own with no signal. No world existed to quit from and none was created.
profilingReObservationCampaign.launcherNote: Prism is single-instance and none was running when this launch started. It was launched with the instance id on the command line and the account taken from its own state, which is not recorded here.
profilingReObservationCampaign.instanceConfigurationRestoredDetail: `OverrideJavaArgs`, `JvmArgs`, `WrapperCommand`, `OverrideCommands`, and `ShowConsole` were captured before the launch and written back afterwards from that capture, then read back and compared field by field. The launcher rewrites its own instance file on exit, so the read-back is what establishes the restore rather than the write.
profilingReObservationCampaign.whatThisDoesNotClaim: It does not claim the surface campaign's rows, the world round trip, or that M3-W8 closes. It answers one blocking finding by binding one reading to one hashed build. `review.result` stays `fail` and the blocking risk stays in place, because whether M3 closes is a sixth independent review's decision and not this campaign's.

The redacted log is the sanitized form of the same stream, with the home directory prefix and the player name replaced; both digests are recorded so a later reader can tell what was hashed. No launcher path, instance path, account material, or full launch command is recorded anywhere in this file.
